transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
President Trump is reacting negatively, at least at first, to news of Democrats' broad
wins in midterm elections yesterday.
The president blamed Republican candidates initially.
He found fault with Fox News.
On his social media page, the president has a large image of his traditional red hat,
with the word "vito" emblazoned on it.
The president later congratulated Democrats on their victory.
But NPR's Franco Ordonez reports, President Trump is likely to face off against Democrats
in the upcoming Congress.
I think we can expect that Trump is going to be pretty confrontational going forward,
especially with the relationship with Democrats.
I mean, Democrats are expected to launch all sorts of investigations of Trump and his family.
And Trump has signaled that he will continue to flex his executive powers, as he already
has.
But he did also say that he will make some deals, and you saw a little hint of that attitude
with his willingness to congratulate Democrats.
He did do the same thing back in 2018 during his first term, though things did eventually
turn somewhat contentious.
So it is a bit of a wait-and-see moment.
NPR's Franco Ordonez is reporting.
Democrats won a number of congressional seats that were redrawn ahead of this year's midterm
elections.
Republicans tried to blunt the effects of a wave election, but NPR's Ashley Lopez reports
those efforts failed in several cases.
Democrats won congressional districts that were redrawn by the GOP for the explicit purpose
of giving their party an edge in this year's election.
Republicans were bracing for some losses this cycle, so President Trump urged his party
to take the extraordinary step of engaging in mid-decade redistricting efforts.
But in Florida, North Carolina, Alabama and Texas, Democrats were able to win many of
those redrawn districts.
Republicans redrew their maps with the expectation that the coalition of voters who Trump won
over in 2024 would support him this cycle.
But many of those voters shifted their support to Democrats this year.
Ashley Lopez, NPR News.
Iranian officials are reacting to the U.S. midterm election results.
The top Iranian negotiator says these show Americans reject a possible return to war.
And P.S.
Hadil Al-Shelchi reports.
"The Iranian speaker of parliament, Mohammad Khalibaf, said that whether it was out of
conscience or the pressure of living expenses, Americans said no to the war, and that Iranians
confirmed this message.
According to Iranian state media, Khalibaf, who is also one of Iran's main negotiators,
said that if the U.S. "betrays" its public and goes to war, it will face a "nightmare"
from Iran.
Iran used its closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway for oil and gas shipping,
to keep gas prices high, pursuing this strategy to try to anger President Trump's base, hoping
it would help cost his party the midterm elections.
NPR's Hadil Al-Shelchi reporting.
This is NPR.
There were few hiccups reported at polling sites yesterday.
There were weather-related problems in Florida.
Several Florida polling stations had to be relocated after torrential rain flooded or
damaged some polling stations.
Big tech company Google says it's making changes to its education software.
It says this will give schools more control over artificial intelligence tools.
But NPR's Sequoia Carillo reports there's one large caveat.
Google Classroom, the dominant software suite used by more than 100 million students, will
now give schools the option to turn off AI.
The features in question mostly revolve around the company's flagship chatbot Gemini, but
this announcement also says that if schools decide they do not want AI, Google Search
would be disabled entirely.
The move comes as school districts around the country are reevaluating the way technology
operates in classrooms.
The two largest in the country, the Los Angeles Unified School District and New York City
Public Schools, recently announced limitations around AI and screen time for students.
Google says the changes will roll out in the coming months.
Sequoia Carillo, NPR News.
Google is among NPR's financial supporters.
The central bank in Paraguay has seized a major digital bank with close ties to Paraguayan
president Santiago Pena.
It's thrown hundreds of millions of dollars into limbo that belong to customers and to
Paraguayan public funds.
Paraguayan authorities say the digital bank appears to be failing.
Prosecutors have ordered arrests.
You're listening to NPR.

topics.text: Trump reacts negatively at first to Democrats' midterm wins, later congratulates them
Trump likely to face confrontation with Democrats in upcoming Congress, NPR's Franco Ordonez reports
Democrats win redrawn GOP congressional districts in Florida, North Carolina, Alabama and Texas
Iran's parliament speaker says Americans rejected war in midterm results, warns of nightmare
Some Florida polling stations relocated after torrential rain flooded or damaged them
Google Classroom lets schools turn off AI features, including Gemini, and even Google Search
Central bank in Paraguay seizes major digital bank tied to President Santiago Pena, freezing funds
